Interface EntityFactory

All Known Implementing Classes:
J2dEntityFactory
public interface EntityFactory
Abstract Factory interface for creating all game entities.

This interface is the heart of the game/visualization separation:

  • It lives in the game package (pure logic, no awt imports).
  • It is implemented in the j2d package (J2dEntityFactory).
  • The Game singleton only ever holds an EntityFactory reference — it never knows which concrete implementation is behind it.

How it works: Main creates a J2dEntityFactory and passes it to Game.start(). From that point on, every entity the game creates (towers, enemies, projectiles, etc.) goes through this interface. The returned objects are typed as abstract game entities (Tower, Enemy, …) so the game loop never touches J2d-specific code.

Swapping visualizations: to replace Java2D with any other renderer, create a new class that implements EntityFactory and pass it to Game.start() instead. Zero changes to the game logic package are required.

    • createCannonProjectile

      Projectile createCannonProjectile(Position start, Position targetPos, int damage, double splashRadius, int splashDamage)
      Creates a cannon projectile that, on impact, deals direct damage to its primary target and splash damage to all other enemies within splashRadius. The splash logic lives in the projectile (CannonProjectile.onHit), not in the game loop.
      Parameters:
      start - the position the projectile is fired from
      targetPos - the world position the projectile flies toward
      damage - the direct-hit damage
      splashRadius - the splash radius in game-world units
      splashDamage - the damage applied to other enemies within the splash radius
      Returns:
      the newly created projectile
